Here is my workaround wrapper script.
[celery-wrapper.py.txt](https://github.com/celery/celery/files/2998317/celery-wrapper.py.txt)
please send a PR with the fix and test.

The PIDfile is not owned by a different user.  The problem is that the code assumes kill() will set errno to ESRCH if the process does not exist but that only works if it is running as root.  For a non-privileged user, kill() sometimes sets errno to EPERM if there is no such process.

issue.title: #5409: remove stale pidfile for non privileged user
issue.body: FIx for #5409.  In addition to checking ESRCH, also check for kill returning/throwing EPERM.

issue.title: Work around Celery bug #5409 leaving stale pid files
issue.body:
When stopping the app docker container, stale pid files are left by [Celery bug #5409](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/5409). These prevent normal startup of the celery workers on a restart, resulting in a time-out of celery-ping.sh and unsuccessful container startup.

This is supposedly fixed in Celery 4.4.0. For now, work around the issue by removing stale pid files in `entrypoint.sh`.
